subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up - Acme.ai
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up - Acme.ai

Hi Jane,

Great to meet you earlier — thanks for walking through Acme.ai's use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of requirements (from our call):
- Primary product: real-time document summarization in support chat (user-facing).
- Latency target: median <200ms tail <500ms for single-turn queries.
- Expected volume: ~120M tokens/month initially, with peak hourly spikes ~10x baseline during product launches.
- Security/data residency: customer PII, must meet SOC 2 controls; prefer data-stay-in-us.
- Timeline: pilot in Sept, procurement/PO by end of Oct if pilot looks good.

Deployment modes we discussed (pros/cons high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to ship, pay-as-you-go per-token. Good for spike flexibility but unit cost is higher and less isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool (monthly commit) giving predictable throughput and lower per-token unit economics for steady state. Autoscaling/burst options available.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — for strict isolation/data residency. Longer lead time and higher fixed platform fees.

Action items / next steps I recommend:
- I will put together a short cost model showing per-token hosted pricing vs a 12/24-month dedicated commit example and a schematic for a private VPC deployment.
- Please confirm expected steady-state tokens/month and anticipated peak concurrency so I can size dedicated capacity appropriately.
- If procurement needs an SOW or security evidence, I can loop in our security team and attach SOC2/controls docs.

I've attached a one-page Redwood_pricing_summary.pdf with baseline hosted vs dedicated numbers and will follow up tomorrow with a tailored cost model.

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up Thurs (Aug 20) to review the cost model and sizing?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (1 page)

From: Jane Park <jane@acme.ai>

Cc: Acme.ai Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up - Acme.ai

Thanks Aditya — good recap. A few clarifications: 

- Steady-state: we expect ~120M tokens/month as you noted, but our roadmap expects 6-8x growth over 12 months if retention improves.
- Peaks: our last launch hit ~12x baseline for a 3-hour window, so any dedicated sizing should consider burst capacity.
- Security: SOC 2 + data residency in US is required; we'll need your SOC2 report and an indication of what logs/audit data you retain.

We're leaning toward Dedicated for cost predictability, but we need to see the committed capacity economics vs hosted before committing. Also, procurement will want to see a sample pricing/commit worksheet and an example contract term (term lengths, termination clauses, SLAs).

Can you send the cost model and a sample contract draft? We can do the Thurs call — 11am PT works for me.

Thanks,
Jane
Head of Product, Acme.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Acme.ai Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode + pricing follow-up - Acme.ai

Jane — thanks, attached is the tailored cost model and two supporting docs: Acmeai_cost_model_v1.xlsx and Redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf. Below is a concise summary tuned to the numbers you gave.

Assumptions used in the attached model:
- Steady-state tokens/month: 120M
- Growth: 6x over 12 months modeled separately tab
- Avg token length per request: 120 tokens (prompt + response)
- Peak concurrency window modeled as 12x baseline for sizing burst pool

Summary (high level):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.0008 per token (example rate) -> ~ $96k/month at 120M tokens. Pros: zero infra commit, simple procurement. Cons: higher unit cost at scale and less control over data residency if you need Private.
- Dedicated capacity (monthly reserved commit): example commit of 200K tokens/sec equivalent capacity with burst pool -> estimated billing $42k/month for commit (12-mo term) + variable overage at lower unit rates. This yields ~55% cost savings vs hosted at steady-state volumes. Includes SLA, priority capacity, and prefix caching optimizations.
- Private VPC/on-prem: significant one-time onboarding + platform fee (we quoted ~ $250k initial setup + monthly infra costs). Best for strict isolation and long-term large scale.

Notes on procurement terms:
- We can do 12- or 24-month committed terms. Longer terms reduce commit price and allow larger discounts.
- Contract template attached includes standard termination for convenience, data residency clauses, and an SLA section (99.9% uptime target for Dedicated).

Next steps I propose:
1) Review the attached cost model with your finance/procurement on Thurs 11am PT — I'll include our solutions architect and pricing lead.
2) If Dedicated looks like the right fit, we can mock a 12-mo commit agreement and provide a refined SKU-level quote within 48 hours.
3) For SOC 2/docs, I'll loop in security (see related link) and provide the report ahead of the pilot.

Quoted attachments: Acmeai_cost_model_v1.xlsx; Redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf
